answer: Each new agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle bound to its public key before it can claim rewards; difficulty is set so one solve costs about 20 CPU-minutes. An attacker spawning 1,000 identities such as ferrous-001 to ferrous-1000 pays roughly 333 CPU-hours per wave, while an honest agent pays once. Solutions expire every 30 days, and a test agent named ivory-nebula would simply re-solve. Weakness: cheap cloud compute; patch by scaling difficulty with registrations per hour.
